questions.question: What does the append() method do to a Python list?
options: A) Adds an element to the end
questions.explanation: append() adds a single element to the end of the list. pop() removes, sort() sorts, reverse() reverses.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about TCP?
options: A) TCP is faster than UDP for real-time streaming
B) TCP is connectionless and unreliable
C) TCP does not guarantee delivery
D) TCP provides connection-oriented, reliable, ordered delivery
questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented (3-way handshake), reliable (acknowledgments, retransmissions), and guarantees ordered delivery. UDP is connectionless and faster for streaming.

questions.question: Which of the following sorting algorithms is stable?
questions.explanation: Bubble Sort is stable — equal elements are never swapped past each other. Quick Sort, Heap Sort, and Selection Sort are generally not stable.

questions.question: What does DDL stand for in database terminology?
questions.explanation: DDL = Data Definition Language. It includes CREATE, ALTER, DROP commands. DML includes SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following Python code?
print(type([]))
questions.explanation: In Python, [] creates an empty list. type([]) returns <class 'list'>.

questions.question: What is the tightest lower bound for comparison-based sorting algorithms in the worst case?
questions.explanation: By the decision-tree model, any comparison-based sort requires at least Ω(n log n) comparisons in the worst case. Merge Sort and Heap Sort achieve this optimal bound.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a firewall?
options: C) Monitor and filter incoming/outgoing network traffic
questions.explanation: A firewall monitors and controls incoming/outgoing network traffic based on security rules, acting as a barrier between trusted and untrusted networks.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to transfer web pages from a server to a browser?
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used for web page transfer. FTP for files, SMTP for email, DNS for domain resolution.

questions.question: Given a DataFrame df, what does df.head() return by default?
questions.explanation: df.head() returns the first 5 rows of the DataFrame. df.tail() returns the last 5 rows. The number can be specified: df.head(n).

questions.question: What is the average-case time complexity of Quick Sort?
questions.explanation: Quick Sort has average-case O(n log n). Worst case is O(n²) when the pivot is consistently the smallest or largest element (e.g., already sorted array with first element as pivot).

questions.question: Given d = {'a': 1, 'b': 2}, what does d.get('c', 0) return?
questions.explanation: dict.get(key, default) returns the value for key if present, otherwise returns the default (0). No KeyError is raised.

questions.question: Given a DataFrame with columns 'Department' and 'Salary', what does df.groupby('Department')['Salary'].mean() return?
options: C) Number of employees per department
questions.explanation: groupby('Department') groups rows by department. ['Salary'].mean() computes the mean of the Salary column for each group. Result: average salary per department.

questions.question: Which networking device forwards data packets between different networks based on IP addresses?
questions.explanation: A Router operates at Layer 3 (Network) and forwards packets between networks using IP addresses. Hubs are Layer 1, Switches are Layer 2, Bridges are Layer 2.

questions.question: An IPv4 address is represented using how many bits?
questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses (e.g., 192.168.1.1). IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.

questions.question: A binary search tree is constructed by inserting the values 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 in that order. What is the height of the resulting tree?
questions.explanation: Inserting: 50(root), 30(left), 70(right), 20(left of 30), 40(right of 30), 60(left of 70), 80(right of 70). All leaves are at depth 2. Height = 2 (max edges from root to leaf).

questions.question: A relation R(A, B, C) has functional dependencies: A → B, A → C. The candidate key is A. What is the highest normal form this relation satisfies?
questions.explanation: Since A is the only candidate key and there are no partial or transitive dependencies (A directly determines B and C), the relation satisfies BCNF. Every determinant (A) is a candidate key.

questions.question: Which encryption method uses the same key for both encryption and decryption?
questions.explanation: Symmetric encryption (AES, DES) uses a single shared key for both encryption and decryption. Asymmetric encryption (RSA) uses a key pair (public/private). Hash functions are one-way.

questions.question: In Python, what is the purpose of the __init__ method in a class?
options: A) To initialize object attributes when an instance is created
B) To convert object to string
questions.explanation: __init__ is the constructor method, automatically called when an object is created to initialize its attributes.

questions.question: In Dijkstra's algorithm, why does it fail to produce correct shortest paths when the graph contains negative edge weights?
options: A) It gets stuck in an infinite loop
B) The greedy choice of the minimum-distance node may be incorrect if a shorter path through negative edges exists
D) It only works for cyclic graphs
questions.explanation: Dijkstra uses a greedy approach, assuming once a node's shortest distance is finalized, it cannot be improved. Negative edges can invalidate this assumption by creating shorter paths to already-finalized nodes.

questions.question: How many layers does the OSI reference model have?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to prevent SQL injection attacks?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate SQL code from data, preventing malicious input from being interpreted as SQL commands. Input validation alone is not sufficient.

questions.question: In a circular queue implementation using an array of size N, how is the rear pointer updated during enqueue?
questions.explanation: Circular queue uses modular arithmetic: rear = (rear + 1) % N. This wraps the pointer around to the beginning when it reaches the end.

questions.question:
Consider tables Employees(EmpID, Name, DeptID) and Departments(DeptID, DeptName). What does the following SQL return?
SELECT * FROM Employees LEFT JOIN Departments ON Employees.DeptID = Departments.DeptID;
options: A) All rows from both tables with NULLs where no match
B) All rows from Employees, with matching department data or NULL
C) Only matching rows from both tables
D) Only rows where DeptID is NULL
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN returns all rows from the left table (Employees) and matching rows from the right table (Departments). If no match, NULL is returned for Departments columns.

questions.question: A network has subnet mask 255.255.255.224. How many usable host addresses are available per subnet?
questions.explanation: Mask 255.255.255.224 = /27 (27 bits for network, 5 bits for hosts). 2^5 = 32 total addresses. Minus 2 (network + broadcast) = 30 usable hosts.

questions.question: Which error detection technique uses polynomial division to generate a checksum?
questions.explanation: CRC uses polynomial division (divisor = generator polynomial). The remainder becomes the checksum. Parity check uses bit counting, checksum uses addition, Hamming uses multiple parity bits.

questions.question: In bubble sort, after the first pass over an array of n elements, which element is guaranteed to be in its correct position?
questions.explanation: In each pass of bubble sort, adjacent elements are compared and swapped if out of order. After the first pass, the largest element 'bubbles up' to the last position.

questions.question: In pandas, the merge() function with how='inner' returns:
options: A) All rows from the left DataFrame
B) All rows from both DataFrames
C) Only rows with matching keys in both DataFrames
D) All rows from the right DataFrame
questions.explanation: how='inner' returns only rows where the key exists in BOTH DataFrames (intersection). 'left' keeps all left rows, 'right' keeps all right rows, 'outer' keeps all rows from both.

questions.question: Heap Sort primarily uses which data structure?
questions.explanation: Heap Sort builds a max-heap (or min-heap) from the array. A heap is a complete binary tree where each parent is ≥ (or ≤) its children. The root is repeatedly extracted.

questions.question: Which port number is used by HTTPS by default?
questions.explanation: HTTPS uses port 443 by default. HTTP uses 80. SSH uses 22. 8080 is an alternative HTTP port.

questions.question: Interpolation search works best when the array elements are:
questions.explanation: Interpolation search estimates the position of the target using linear interpolation. It achieves O(log log n) average time for uniformly distributed sorted data, but degrades to O(n) otherwise.
This is the Fibonacci function. f(0)=0, f(1)=1, f(2)=1, f(3)=2, f(4)=3, f(5)=5, f(6)=8. The 6th Fibonacci number is 8.

questions.question: A table Students(StudentID, Name, Marks). Which query correctly finds the student(s) with the second highest marks?
options: A) SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Marks = MAX(Marks)
B) SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Marks > (SELECT AVG(Marks) FROM Students)
C) SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Marks = (SELECT MAX(Marks) FROM Students WHERE Marks < (SELECT MAX(Marks) FROM Students))
D) SELECT Name FROM Students WHERE Marks = (SELECT MIN(Marks) FROM Students)
questions.explanation: To find all students with the second highest marks (including handling ties properly), a nested subquery determines the maximum marks strictly less than the overall maximum marks: (SELECT MAX(Marks) FROM Students WHERE Marks < (SELECT MAX(Marks) FROM Students)). The outer query then retrieves every student whose Marks match this value. Aggregate functions cannot be used directly in a WHERE clause without a subquery, filtering above average retrieves multiple different scores, and using MIN() retrieves students with the lowest marks.

questions.question: Which property of ACID ensures that either all operations of a transaction are executed or none at all?
questions.explanation: Atomicity ensures all-or-nothing execution. Consistency ensures valid state transitions. Isolation ensures concurrent transactions don't interfere. Durability ensures committed data persists.

questions.question: What is a phishing attack?
options: B) Overloading a server with traffic
C) Tricking users into revealing sensitive information via deceptive messages
questions.explanation: Phishing uses deceptive emails/messages to trick users into revealing passwords, credit card info, or clicking malicious links.

questions.question: What is the best-case time complexity of linear search on an array of n elements?
questions.explanation: Best case: target element is found at the first position, requiring only 1 comparison = O(1).

questions.question:
What does the following pandas operation return?
df.pivot_table(values='Sales', index='Region', columns='Quarter', aggfunc='sum')
options: A) A pivot table with Region as rows, Quarter as columns, and sum of Sales as values
B) A single column of total sales
C) A sorted list of sales
questions.explanation: pivot_table reshapes data: index='Region' creates row labels, columns='Quarter' creates column labels, values='Sales' provides the data, aggfunc='sum' aggregates by summation. Result is a 2D summary table.

questions.question: A PRIMARY KEY constraint in SQL ensures that the column(s):
options: A) Must be unique but can be NULL
B) Must be unique and cannot be NULL
C) Cannot be unique and can be NULL
D) Cannot be unique but cannot be NULL
questions.explanation: PRIMARY KEY enforces both UNIQUE and NOT NULL constraints. A table can have only one primary key.

questions.question:
A router has the following routing entries:
192.168.0.0/16 via Interface A
192.168.10.0/24 via Interface B
192.168.10.128/25 via Interface C
If a packet arrives for 192.168.10.200, which interface is used?
questions.explanation: Longest prefix matching is used. 192.168.10.200 matches all three entries but /25 (Interface C) is the longest (most specific) prefix. The router selects the most specific match.

questions.question: What does the pandas function read_csv() return?
questions.explanation: pd.read_csv() reads a CSV file and returns a pandas DataFrame — a 2D labeled data structure with columns of potentially different types.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in an array by index?
questions.explanation: Array access by index is O(1) because the memory address is calculated directly: base_address + index × element_size.

questions.question: In RSA encryption, the public key consists of (e, n). What does the private key consist of?
options: A) (p, q) where p and q are the prime factors
C) (d, n) where d is the modular multiplicative inverse of e modulo φ(n)
questions.explanation: RSA private key is (d, n) where d ≡ e⁻¹ (mod φ(n)), i.e., e·d ≡ 1 (mod φ(n)). Knowing (p,q) allows computing d but the private key stored is (d,n).

questions.question: What does the following SQL query return? SELECT COUNT(*) FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);
options: A) Number of employees earning more than the average salary
B) Average salary of all employees
C) Sum of salaries above average
questions.explanation: The subquery computes the average salary. The outer query counts employees whose salary exceeds that average. COUNT(*) counts all rows matching the condition.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm is based on the divide-and-conquer paradigm?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort divides the array into halves, recursively sorts each half, then merges them. It's the classic divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm.

questions.question: In TCP congestion control, what happens to the congestion window size when packet loss is detected during the congestion avoidance phase?
options: C) It is set to 1 MSS
questions.explanation: During congestion avoidance, TCP uses AIMD (Additive Increase, Multiplicative Decrease). On packet loss (detected by timeout or 3 duplicate ACKs), the window is halved (multiplicative decrease). Setting to 1 MSS occurs on timeout (entering slow start).

questions.question: Binary search requires the input array to be:
questions.explanation: Binary search works by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half. This requires the array to be sorted (ascending or descending).

questions.question: Consider a B+ tree index on a column with 10,000 distinct values. The leaf nodes contain pointers to data pages. Which statement is TRUE about range queries?
options: A) Range queries require scanning the entire table
B) Only exact-match queries benefit from B+ tree
C) B+ tree index is inefficient for range queries
D) B+ tree allows efficient range queries by traversing to the start of the range and scanning leaf nodes sequentially
questions.explanation: B+ trees store leaf nodes in sorted linked-list order, enabling efficient range queries. The tree is traversed to find the start key, then leaf nodes are scanned sequentially until the end key is reached.

questions.question: Which data structure follows the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle?
questions.explanation: Stack follows LIFO — the last element pushed is the first popped. Queue follows FIFO.

questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to sort the result set in ascending or descending order?
questions.explanation: ORDER BY is the SQL clause used to sort result sets. ASC for ascending (default), DESC for descending.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of finding the median of an unsorted array of n elements using a comparison-based approach?
questions.explanation: The straightforward approach sorts the array (O(n log n)) then picks the middle element. While linear-time selection algorithms exist (QuickSelect), the question specifies comparison-based approach which implies sorting-based. Even QuickSelect has O(n log n) worst-case with median-of-medians pivot, so O(n log n) is the safe upper bound here.

questions.question: Which SQL command is used to remove all rows from a table without logging individual row deletions (and cannot be rolled back)?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE is a DDL command that deallocates table pages without logging individual row deletions. It cannot be rolled back (in most DBMS). DELETE is DML and can use WHERE and be rolled back.
